questions.q: The editorial holds up Charles De Gaulle as an example. What lesson does it draw from him?
options: Military strength alone makes a nation great
Not quite. The article says: A nation that missed its first chance can re-plan and succeed, if its leaders accept the personal cost.
A nation should never change its first plan
Not quite. The article says: A nation that missed its first chance can re-plan and succeed, if its leaders accept the personal cost.
A leader should guard his popularity above all
Not quite. The article says: A nation that missed its first chance can re-plan and succeed, if its leaders accept the personal cost.
A nation that missed its first chance can re-plan and succeed, if its leaders accept the personal cost
Yes. He lost popularity, but France grew strong.
questions.rationale: “In life it often happens that individuals or nations are unable to avail of the first chance. This is why they have to plan again for a second time.”

questions.q: Every person is born on an upright nature but is shaped by his surroundings. What, then, is tazkiya (purification)?
options: Acquiring new habits from one’s elders
Not quite. The article says: De-conditioning oneself – finding and removing what the environment added – to return to one’s true nature.
Withdrawing from society for good
Not quite. The article says: De-conditioning oneself – finding and removing what the environment added – to return to one’s true nature.
De-conditioning oneself – finding and removing what the environment added – to return to one’s true nature
Right. It is the process of self-correction.
Learning the rules of ritual cleanliness
Not quite. The article says: De-conditioning oneself – finding and removing what the environment added – to return to one’s true nature.
questions.rationale: “Tazkiya or purification is for one to properly understand this problem and to de-condition himself and thereby make himself once again, a person on true nature.”

questions.q: Who, according to the article, can carry out this self-correction for a person?
options: His parents
Not quite. The article says: No one else – it is each person’s own responsibility, through introspection.
A teacher who knows him well
Not quite. The article says: No one else – it is each person’s own responsibility, through introspection.
The community as a whole
Not quite. The article says: No one else – it is each person’s own responsibility, through introspection.
No one else – it is each person’s own responsibility, through introspection
Correct. It begins with searching one’s own mind.
questions.rationale: “This task of self-correction or de-conditioning is not something that someone else can do for another. It is each one's own responsibility.”

questions.q: The sun, the cow and the tree each convert one thing into another. How does the conversion asked of man differ?
options: It is conscious and spiritual – turning observation into knowledge of God, and resentment into forgiveness
Well read. In nature it is instinctive and material.
It needs special equipment
Not quite. The article says: It is conscious and spiritual – turning observation into knowledge of God, and resentment into forgiveness.
It happens only in old age
Not quite. The article says: It is conscious and spiritual – turning observation into knowledge of God, and resentment into forgiveness.
It is quicker than in nature
Not quite. The article says: It is conscious and spiritual – turning observation into knowledge of God, and resentment into forgiveness.
questions.rationale: “In other things, conversion is an instinctive process, whereas in man it is a conscious one; in other things conversion occurs on a material plane, whereas in man it occurs on a spiritual plane.”

questions.q: Japanese shipbuilders finished a tanker in eight months, against sixteen and twenty-four elsewhere. What did the survey find to be the deciding factor?
options: Teamwork – workers and management functioning in complete unison
Yes. Unity is the key to organisational success.
Longer working hours
Not quite. The article says: Teamwork – workers and management functioning in complete unison.
Cheaper materials
Not quite. The article says: Teamwork – workers and management functioning in complete unison.
Newer machinery
Not quite. The article says: Teamwork – workers and management functioning in complete unison.
questions.rationale: “A survey conducted by Western experts shows that the deciding factor is teamwork.”

questions.q: What price does the article say individuals pay in such a system of joint effort?
options: They cannot learn new skills
Not quite. The article says: Their own personality has less room to stand out – a sacrifice a successful nation’s members accept.
They earn lower wages
Not quite. The article says: Their own personality has less room to stand out – a sacrifice a successful nation’s members accept.
They lose touch with their families
Not quite. The article says: Their own personality has less room to stand out – a sacrifice a successful nation’s members accept.
Their own personality has less room to stand out – a sacrifice a successful nation’s members accept
Well reasoned. Group activity is not “a springboard to individual glory.”
questions.rationale: “The only flaw in this system of joint effort is that the personality of the individual has little opportunity to flourish. But it is only a nation which is made up of individuals who are prepared to make this personal sacrifice which can ever aspire to success.”

questions.q: If you come to know of a fault in someone, which two courses does the article approve?
options: Keep it to yourself, or speak to the person privately with compassion
Exactly. “A believer is like a mirror for another believer.”
Ignore him, or report him
Not quite. The article says: Keep it to yourself, or speak to the person privately with compassion.
Warn others about him, or avoid him
Not quite. The article says: Keep it to yourself, or speak to the person privately with compassion.
Announce it publicly, or write to him
Not quite. The article says: Keep it to yourself, or speak to the person privately with compassion.
questions.rationale: “You could keep this fact in your heart and not speak about it to anyone. Or, you could meet this person yourself, and in a spirit of compassion and genuine concern for reform, speak to the person about it.”

questions.q: Why does the article say the approach suited to the freedom struggle needed to change after Independence?
options: Because the old leaders had retired
Not quite. The article says: The relationship was now between Indians and Indians, which calls for duty-consciousness rather than demands for rights.
Because foreign countries required it
Not quite. The article says: The relationship was now between Indians and Indians, which calls for duty-consciousness rather than demands for rights.
The relationship was now between Indians and Indians, which calls for duty-consciousness rather than demands for rights
Yes. A better society is a duty-conscious one.
Because rights no longer mattered to anyone
Not quite. The article says: The relationship was now between Indians and Indians, which calls for duty-consciousness rather than demands for rights.
questions.rationale: “In the post-Independence period, the equation was between Indians and Indians. Now it has become essential to change our strategy from being rights-based to being duty-based.”

questions.q: At Geneva airport the author spoke to a traveller about “cow culture.” What did he mean?
options: Keeping to a simple diet
Not quite. The article says: Converting negative experiences into positive thinking, as a cow turns non-milk into milk.
Honouring animals in ritual
Not quite. The article says: Converting negative experiences into positive thinking, as a cow turns non-milk into milk.
Converting negative experiences into positive thinking, as a cow turns non-milk into milk
Right. She resolved to give up the complaint culture.
Living close to the land
Not quite. The article says: Converting negative experiences into positive thinking, as a cow turns non-milk into milk.
questions.rationale: “The cow is a natural ‘industry’ which converts what is non-milk into milk. This is a demonstration by nature telling humans to adopt the cow culture by converting negativity into positivity.”

questions.q: Neighbouring plots fed by the same water bear fruits of different taste (13:4). What human parallel does the commentary draw?
options: Sweet fruit grows only with more water
Not quite. The article says: The same guidance is offered to all, yet people benefit from it very differently.
Good soil is a matter of luck
Not quite. The article says: The same guidance is offered to all, yet people benefit from it very differently.
People of different lands need different guidance
Not quite. The article says: The same guidance is offered to all, yet people benefit from it very differently.
The same guidance is offered to all, yet people benefit from it very differently
Well read. One is enriched; another takes little.
questions.rationale: “The same ‘seeds’ of guidance when ‘sown’ in different individuals will produce outcomes as different as the sweet and sour fruits of our analogy.”
